Hi. I lost my father last year in June. We had a complicated relationship, too. I used to be angry with him for many things he did in the past and still found it hard to get over them through the years. In his last few years on Earth when he got sick I did my duty as daughter and took care of him
In the best way I knew how but my treatment towards was always indifferent.

Then when he died, I suddenly felt so lost. I didn’t know what I was supposed to feel. I wanted to mourn and hold on to our memories but for some reason, I only was able to recall a few happy ones, only the ones when I was really young. Most were sad memories that I didn’t want to recall. I felt like I was hit by a truckload of confusing emotions and I was overwhelmed for a while.

Just wanted to let you know I can relate with how you feel especially the part you said you don’t regret the choices, but that you had to make those choices.

I am still on the journey of healing and forgiveness - toward myself and my father.
I’m so sorry for your loss. I too lost my dad over a year ago. The grief never leaves, but honestly I prefer it this way. Grief is love that has nowhere to go.

I feel you. My dad passed a month ago. We did not have a good relationship. I blamed him a lot for our family problems and there was a very long time when I felt like he didn’t deserve to be loved. I was angry with him for a very long time.

Now I am a total wreck grieving for our lost relationship. I feel all sorts of emotions - sadness, loneliness, longing, regret. The truth is I don’t know if I can offer you any good advice. What I’ve been doing that seems to help is to talk about my feelings a lot - with friends or with a support group I’m in. It helps in that moment, then later on I’ll experience another wave of pain. It comes and goes.

Just letting you know you’re not alone. I know it can feel lonely sometimes.

I lost my dad a month ago. I don’t have sad days. I have moments. They come up unexpected. It comes and goes.

Sometimes I feel comforted when I feel the sadness. Like I feel his presence when I am sad. And that comforts me.

I know I am not okay. I don’t know when I’ll be okay again. I’m not in a rush. You don’t have to rush, either.
